A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CstNet and Param20K, and their shared text, equations, tables, and figures are readable. However, v4 includes supplementary Sections F–J, Table 5, and Figures 11–24; v6 ends after its references while still referring to supplementary material. Its supplementary content cannot be compared, and its absence does not establish that the corresponding methods or experiments were deleted.

before.justification: v4 reports original constraint prediction, classification, rotation robustness, and ablation results, including additional MCB results in its supplement.

after.justification: v6 retains original experimental results in Tables 1–4 and Figures 3 and 8–10, and adds classification results for four baselines.

M1.justification: Sections 3.2–3.4 retain the same constraint representation and two-stage CstNet architecture. Figure 7 corrects routing labels to agree with the existing prose, rather than establishing a procedural change. However, v4 specifies MAD canonicalization and SurfaceKNN iterations in Sections J.2 and J.5; their counterparts are deferred to v6's unavailable supplement, preventing a complete procedure comparison.

E1.justification: The shared experiments retain ABC, Param20K, and Prism-Cuboid classification, including rotated Param20K testing. v4 additionally evaluates constraint prediction and classification on MCB in Sections I.3–I.4. v6 refers to supplementary results on other datasets without supplying them, so retention of MCB coverage cannot be determined.

E2.justification: Table 2 substantially broadens the central classification comparison from six to ten baselines by adding HPNet, ParSeNet, Point Transformer V2 (PTV2), and PointMamba (PTMamba). HPNet and ParSeNet already participated in constraint prediction in Table 1, but their classification comparisons are new. The additions introduce CAD-specific methods and further model families into this comparison.

E3.justification: The shared training budget, optimizer settings, ABC pretraining, frozen-CstPnt control, metrics, and rotation procedure match. However, v4's supplement specifies 80/20 splits, 5,000 instances per validation template, and random rotations within ±25 degrees. Corresponding v6 supplementary settings are unavailable, so their retention or revision cannot be verified.

E4.justification: The constraint-component, neighbor-search, and backbone ablations in Tables 3–4 and the rotation analysis in Figure 10 are unchanged. v4 also examines pretrained constraint prediction on unseen MCB shapes in Section I.3 and Figure 18. Without v6's supplement, the status of this additional transfer analysis is unresolved.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added baseline rows retain the existing single-value reporting practice.

E6.justification: Matched table entries and plotted results are unchanged. v6 adds Table 2 accuracies of 83.85% for HPNet, 83.96% for ParSeNet, 85.14% for PTV2, and 86.45% for PTMamba, plus ABC primitive frequencies in Section 3.2. CstNet remains at 89.94%. However, v4's MCB results in Table 5 and Figure 18 lack an available v6 counterpart, preventing a reliable judgment of the complete result-set change.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(2) and the shared positional-encoding definitions match, with no new theorem or proof in the main text. v4's supplementary MAD direction convention and SurfaceKNN locality assumption have no supplied v6 counterpart, so the complete comparison of definitions and assumptions remains uncertain.

C1.justification: The network, representation, dataset, novelty, and generalization contributions retain their scope. The abstract and introduction revise the classification advantage from 3.52 to 3.49 percentage points, reflecting comparison with newly added PTMamba at 86.45% rather than 3DGCN at 86.42%. The stated 26.17-point rotation advantage remains unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 3.2 strengthens the rationale for focusing on planes, cylinders, and cones by reporting their prevalence in one ABC trunk: 69.63%, 17.51%, and 6.99%. v4 primarily justified this choice through their relationship to constraints. The shared interpretations of local-feature generalization, rotation robustness, and failure on 89-degree prisms remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The shared optimizer, hardware, preprocessing description, and project link remain unchanged, and v6 adds an OCCT reference. Important v4 details—including dataset purification, approximately 2,200 points per Param20K instance, splits, MAD canonicalization, and SurfaceKNN implementation—appear in its supplement. Their corresponding v6 documentation is unavailable, preventing a complete reproducibility-information comparison.

R1.justification: v6 adds references including PointMamba, Point Transformer V2, Sketch2seq, Dafu-CAD, Sketch2jewelry, and point-based robot control. The v4 references for Fabsearch, STEP feature recognition, and Q-complex are absent from v6's bibliography. These are limited citation changes; the broad related-work organization and research positioning remain stable.

P1.justification: The abstract and several introduction, method, and experiment paragraphs receive local rewrites and terminology cleanup, particularly around MAD-Adj-PT and constraint representation. v6 also adds an affiliation and acknowledgements and removes bibliographic export metadata. The shared main sections retain their organization.

P2.justification: The main figures retain their content with revised lettering and linework. Figure 7 corrects the reversed CstBRep/CstPnt routing labels, Table 2 gains and reorders rows, and Figures 8–9 move within the main text. The principal layouts and plot designs remain recognizable; supplementary displays cannot be matched.

improvement.justification: v6 improves the main text through broader classification comparisons, a correctly updated performance margin, and corrected routing labels in Figure 7. However, v4 supplies additional MCB validation and substantial reproduction details that cannot be checked against v6's referenced but unavailable supplement. These gaps prevent a reliable assessment of the later paper's overall quality.
